newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CKD SEES CZK 597 MLN 1997 GROSS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CKD SEES CZK 597 MLN 1997 GROSS.

text.p: Czech engineering group CKD Holding a.s. said on Tuesday that it expected consolidated gross profit for 1997 of 597 million crowns after a 924.7 million crown net loss last year.

General Director Jiri Marousek added in a news conference that the company planned to stick to its original privatisation plan and pay its first dividend either on 1997 or 1998 earnings at the latest, but he did not forecast an amount of the possible payout.
He said total sales should grow in 1997 to 12 to 14 billion crowns from just over 10 billion the previous year.
Earlier the company said the loss last year was due in part to the creation of reserves totalling 2.7 billion crowns, and another two billion crowns written off on unpaid receivables from Russia.
"Thanks to a cleansing of the balance sheet last year, the expected positive results will no longer this year be affected by the corrective and past restructuralisation steps," Marousek said.
